# Quickstart

URL: https://konkomaji.github.io/litecode/quickstart.html

# Quickstart

This page takes you from zero to your first task in about 10 minutes, plus model download time.

## 1. Check the requirements

- Python 3.10 or newer: `python --version`. On Windows the installer offers to install it.
- Free disk space: 3 GB for a small PC, 15 GB or more for bigger models

You do not need a GPU. If you have one, litecode uses it.

## 2. Install

Windows (PowerShell):

```
irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/konkomaji/litecode/main/install.ps1 | iex
```

Linux or macOS:

```
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/konkomaji/litecode/main/install.sh | sh
```

The installer adds the `litecode` and `lite` commands to your PATH and starts the setup wizard. If the command is not found afterwards, open a new terminal.

## 3. Answer the setup wizard

The wizard asks 4 things:

1. Where to keep data (cache, memory, skills). Press Enter for the default.
2. Where to keep models. Pick the disk with the most free space.
3. Whether to download the engine. Answer yes. If you have an NVIDIA GPU, answer yes to the CUDA build.
4. Whether to download the recommended models. It shows the size first.

## 4. Tune for your machine

```
litecode tune
```

This takes about 5 minutes. It finds the fastest thread count and decoding mode for your CPU or GPU.

## 5. Run your first task

```
cd path/to/your/project
litecode
```

Type a question or a task:

```
> what is a list comprehension
> explain what @main.py does
> add input validation to the signup function and run the tests
> /review src/
```

Questions get a direct answer. Tasks run the agent. litecode asks before it changes a file or runs a command: pick `1` (yes), `2` (yes for the rest of the session), or `3` (no, and tell it what to do instead). Shift+Tab switches to auto-accept or plan mode.

## 6. Next steps

- Learn the interface and daily commands: [User guide](GUIDE.md)
- See every command: [Commands](COMMANDS.md)
- Pick models for your hardware: [Hardware and models](HARDWARE.md)
- Check how well models do on real tasks: [Benchmarks](BENCHMARKS.md)


---

# litecode guide

URL: https://konkomaji.github.io/litecode/guide.html

# litecode guide

litecode is a local AI coding and security assistant. It runs open-weight models on your own PC. It works offline after setup. Built by Konko Maji.

Contents:
1. Requirements
2. Install
3. Setup
4. First run
5. The interface
6. Daily use
7. Memory and learning
8. Skills
9. MCP servers
10. Security work
11. Speed tuning
12. Files and folders
13. Customize the system prompt
14. Uninstall

Other pages: [Quickstart](QUICKSTART.md), [Commands](COMMANDS.md), [Hardware and models](HARDWARE.md), [Memory and learning](MEMORY.md), [Skills](SKILLS.md), [MCP servers](MCP.md), [Security review](SECURITY.md), [Editor autocomplete](EDITORS.md), [FAQ](FAQ.md), [Troubleshooting](TROUBLESHOOTING.md).

---

## 1. Requirements

| Item | Minimum | Better |
|---|---|---|
| RAM | 4 GB | 16 GB |
| CPU | any x86-64 or ARM64 | 4+ cores with AVX2 |
| Disk | 3 GB free | 15 GB free on an SSD |
| Python | 3.10 | 3.12 |
| GPU | not needed | Vulkan or CUDA GPU (optional) |

litecode has no Python dependencies. It uses only the standard library.

## 2. Install

Windows (PowerShell):

```
irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/konkomaji/litecode/main/install.ps1 | iex
```

Linux or macOS:

```
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/konkomaji/litecode/main/install.sh | sh
```

The installer does these steps:

1. It finds Python 3.10 or newer. On Windows it offers to install Python with winget if none is found.
2. It creates a private Python environment: `%LOCALAPPDATA%\litecode` (Windows) or `~/.local/share/litecode` (Linux, macOS).
3. It installs litecode there and adds the `litecode` and `lite` commands to your PATH.
4. It starts `litecode setup`. Set `LITECODE_NO_SETUP=1` to skip this step.

From a clone, run `.\install.ps1` or `sh install.sh` in the repo folder. This makes an editable install, so code changes apply at once.

If the `litecode` command is not found after install, open a new terminal.

Update: `litecode update`. Uninstall: delete the private environment folder. Models and data stay in the folders you picked.

## 3. Setup

Run:

```
litecode setup
```

The wizard does these steps:

1. It detects CPU, RAM, disks (SSD or HDD) and GPU.
2. It asks where to keep data. Data = cache, KV slots, scratchpad, memory, skills. Press Enter to use the default (`~/.litecode`).
3. It asks where to keep models. Models need several GB. Pick the disk with the most free space.
4. It asks if project memory goes in each project (`.litecode/` folder) or in the data folder.
5. It downloads the llama.cpp engine (30-80 MB) if no engine is found.
6. It recommends models that fit your RAM. It shows the download size and asks before it downloads.
7. It writes `~/.litecode/config.toml`.

Then run the tuner once (about 5 minutes):

```
litecode tune
```

The tuner measures thread counts and speculative decoding on your PC. It saves the fastest settings.

To change a location later: run `litecode setup` again, or `litecode config data_dir D:/litecode-data`.

## 4. First run

```
cd my-project
litecode init        # optional: creates LITECODE.md, a brief about the project
litecode
```

The first model load takes 10-60 seconds on a hard drive. Later tasks reuse the loaded model.

One task without the interactive screen:

```
litecode "add a --json flag to main.py and update the tests"
```

## 5. The interface

```
╭────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ ✻ Welcome to litecode  v0.2.0                          │
│                                                        │
│ /help for help, /status for your setup                 │
│                                                        │
│ cwd:   C:\code\my-project                              │
│ model: MiniCPM5-2B-Q4_K_M · CPU 4 threads              │
╰────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯

> fix the failing test in @tests/test_api.py
  read the test first
● Read(tests/test_api.py)
  ⎿  Read 24 lines
● Update(api.py)
╭─ Edit file ──────────────────────────────────────────
│   api.py
│   - return a - b
│   + return a + b
│
│ Do you want to proceed?
│ ❯ 1. Yes
│   2. Yes, and allow all edits this session
│   3. No, and tell litecode what to do differently (esc)
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  ⎿  Updated api.py (1 replacement)
● Bash(python -m pytest -q)
  ⎿  exit 0
     3 passed in 0.12s
● The test failed because add() subtracted. I changed line 2 of api.py. All tests pass.
  · 412 tokens · 38s · MiniCPM5-2B-Q4_K_M
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
>
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  ? for shortcuts · MiniCPM5-2B-Q4_K_M
```

Line types:

| Mark | Meaning |
|---|---|
| grey text | the model's short reasoning for the next step |
| `● Name(...)` | a tool call: Read, Write, Update, Bash, List, Search, Git, Scan |
| `⎿` | the result of the tool call, shortened |
| red `-` / green `+` | lines removed / added by an edit |
| `●` + text | the answer, streamed live |
| last line | tokens, seconds, model |

While the model works, a spinner shows the time and the token count. Press Ctrl+C to stop.

Questions and greetings ("what is a list comprehension") get a direct answer without tools, in a few seconds. Tasks ("create calc.py", "fix the bug in app.py") run the agent.

Input keys:

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Enter | send |
| `\` then Enter | new line |
| Up / Down | message history |
| Tab | complete a `/command` |
| Shift+Tab | cycle mode: ask, auto-accept, plan |
| Esc | clear the input |
| Ctrl+C | stop a task; on an empty input, press twice to exit |
| `?` | show shortcuts |

Input prefixes: `@path/file` attaches a file, `!command` runs a shell command at once (its output becomes context), `#text` saves a project fact.

Modes: **ask** asks before each change. **auto-accept** applies changes without asking. **plan** inspects only and writes a plan, then asks if it should carry it out. `/mode readonly` refuses all changes.

## 6. Daily use

| Goal | Type |
|---|---|
| Ask or change code | plain text |
| Plan first, no edits | `/plan add caching to the API` |
| Run tests and fix | `/test` or `/test npm test` |
| Security review | `/review src/` |
| Fast static scan only | `/scan` |
| Commit message | `/commit` |
| Undo an edit | `/undo path/file.py` (repeat to step back further) |
| See token use | `/cost` |
| Rate the last answer | `/good` or `/bad` |

Permission modes (`/mode`):

| Mode | Behavior |
|---|---|
| `ask` | litecode asks before each edit or command (default) |
| `auto` | no questions; same as `--yes` |
| `readonly` | edits and commands are refused |

All commands: [Commands](COMMANDS.md).

## 7. Memory and learning

litecode records every session to disk automatically. It learns without retraining the model:

1. Preferences: if you write "always use type hints" or "don't add comments", litecode saves it. It applies to all projects.
2. Facts: when a session ends, the model writes short project facts (commands, conventions). A test command that passes is saved at once.
3. Examples: each finished task is stored. A similar task later gets the best past answer as an example. `/good` and `/bad` rate answers. Bad answers are never reused.

You can see and edit all of it: `/memory`, `/forget`, and the files listed in [Memory and learning](MEMORY.md).

Real fine-tuning: `litecode learn export data.jsonl` writes your rated history as a training set. Train a LoRA on a GPU machine. Set `lora` in config. Details in [Memory and learning](MEMORY.md).

## 8. Skills

A skill is a saved instruction pack, like a Claude Code skill. Built-in skills: `review`, `test-fix`, `explain`, `commit`, `refactor`, `skill-builder`.

- Run one: `/review src/`, `/explain @utils.py`.
- Make one step by step: `/skill new my-skill`.
- Let the model draft one: `/skill make a skill that checks Django migrations`.
- List: `/skills`.

Details: [Skills](SKILLS.md).

## 9. MCP servers

litecode connects to Model Context Protocol servers over stdio. It reads the same `.mcp.json` format as Claude Code.

```
litecode mcp add fs npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem .
litecode mcp            # list servers
```

Inside a session, `/mcp` lists the tools. Details: [MCP servers](MCP.md).

Warning: small models handle few tools well. Add only the servers you need.

## 10. Security work

- `/scan` runs static rules with no model. If Semgrep or Bandit is installed, litecode uses them too.
- `/review` scans, then the model gives a verdict for each finding: real or false positive, severity, reason, fix.
- Reports are saved in `.litecode/reviews/`.
- The setup can install an official security model (Foundation-Sec-8B or WhiteRabbitNeo). Security tasks route to it.

Use security features only on code and systems you own or have permission to test.

## 11. Speed tuning

| Setting | Effect |
|---|---|
| `litecode tune` | picks threads and speculative mode by measurement |
| `kv_persist = true` | saves the prompt cache per project; next start skips reprocessing |
| `speculative = "auto"` | n-gram drafting for code roles; it speeds up edits that repeat text |
| `ctx = 8192` | smaller context = less RAM, faster |
| `gpu_layers = 99` | with a Vulkan or CUDA engine build, moves layers to the GPU |
| models on SSD | load time drops from about 30 s to about 5 s |

Generation speed depends mostly on RAM bandwidth. Two RAM sticks (dual channel) are about 2x faster than one.

## 12. Files and folders

| Path | Content |
|---|---|
| `~/.litecode/config.toml` | settings |
| `<data_dir>/profile.jsonl` | your preferences (all projects) |
| `<data_dir>/learn/examples.jsonl` | finished tasks with ratings |
| `<data_dir>/slots/` | saved prompt caches |
| `<data_dir>/scratch/` | scratchpad files |
| `<data_dir>/skills/` | your user skills |
| `<data_dir>/mcp.json` | your MCP servers |
| `<data_dir>/bench/` | tune reports |
| `<project>/LITECODE.md` | project brief (you edit it) |
| `<project>/.litecode/` | project facts, sessions, summaries, checkpoints, reviews, project skills |

## 13. Customize the system prompt

litecode ships `litecode/SYSTEM.md`. It holds the tool protocol and the answer style rules (ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English: answer first, short sentences, exact values, no filler).

To change it, copy it to `<data_dir>/SYSTEM.md` and edit the copy. Keep the `{spec}` line: litecode puts the tool list there.

## 14. Uninstall

1. `pip uninstall litecode`
2. Delete `~/.litecode` and your data and models folders.
3. Delete `.litecode/` folders in your projects.


---

# Hardware and models

URL: https://konkomaji.github.io/litecode/hardware.html

# Hardware and models

litecode runs on any machine, from a 4 GB laptop to a workstation with a large GPU. It measures the machine and picks models that fit. On a small PC it picks small, fast models. On a big machine it picks bigger, stronger models.

## How litecode chooses

1. `litecode setup` reads total RAM, CPU cores, disk type, and GPU.
2. It plans with about 60% of total RAM, so your browser and editor keep working.
3. It picks a model for each role: `code`, `chat`, `fim` (autocomplete), `security`, and `quality` (hard tasks).
4. With a GPU build, it moves model layers to the GPU (`gpu_layers = 99`).

## Tiers

| Machine | What litecode loads | Expected use |
|---|---|---|
| 4 GB RAM, no GPU | Qwen2.5-Coder-1.5B + 0.5B autocomplete | code help, explanations, small fixes |
| 8 GB RAM, no GPU | MiniCPM5-2B + 1.5B autocomplete | daily coding, security review, writing |
| 16 GB RAM, no GPU | LFM2.5-8B-A1B (fast MoE) + security model on demand | full agent work on real projects |
| 32 GB RAM | adds Qwen3.5-9B as the quality model | harder multi-file tasks |
| GPU, 12 GB+ VRAM | Qwen3.6-35B-A3B and other 30B-class models | large refactors, deep reviews, long context |

These are defaults. Any GGUF model works. Set it with `litecode config roles.code MyModel.gguf`.

## GPUs

| GPU | Engine build | How to get it |
|---|---|---|
| NVIDIA | CUDA | setup offers it when it finds `nvidia-smi` |
| AMD, Intel, NVIDIA | Vulkan | setup offers it when it finds `vulkaninfo` |
| Apple Silicon | Metal (in the macOS build) | automatic |
| Old GPUs (2 GB, Kepler era) | CPU | litecode ignores the GPU |

Set how many layers go to the GPU: `litecode config gpu_layers 99` (all) or a smaller number to share VRAM.

## What makes it fast

- Generation speed depends mostly on memory bandwidth. Two RAM sticks (dual channel) give about 2x the speed of one.
- Models on an SSD load in about 5 seconds. On a hard drive they take about 30 seconds. litecode keeps the model loaded between tasks.
- The prompt cache is saved per project. The next session skips reprocessing the long system prompt.
- N-gram speculative decoding speeds up edits that repeat existing code.
- `litecode tune` measures all of this on your machine and keeps the fastest settings.

## Reference machine

All published litecode numbers come from this low-end PC, so you can compare:

| Part | Value |
|---|---|
| CPU | AMD Ryzen 3 3200G, 4 cores, 4 threads (2019) |
| RAM | 16 GB DDR4-2133, dual channel |
| GPU | GeForce GT 710 2 GB (too old, not used) |
| Disk | 7200 rpm hard drive for models |

If litecode runs well on this machine, it runs better on yours. See [Benchmarks](BENCHMARKS.md).


---

# Use cases

URL: https://konkomaji.github.io/litecode/use-cases.html

# Use cases

litecode focuses on coding and security. It also helps with writing, study, and everyday questions, because the same local models do those tasks well.

## Coding (main focus)

- Fix bugs: "test_cart.py fails, find the root cause and fix it."
- Add features with tests: "add a --json flag and update the tests."
- Refactor safely: "rename get_usr to get_user in every file." litecode runs the tests before and after.
- Explain code: "explain @parser.py step by step."
- Test-fix loop: `/test` runs your tests, reads the failure, fixes the code, and runs them again.
- Commit messages: `/commit` writes a message from the diff.
- Autocomplete in your editor: `litecode fim`.

## Security (main focus)

- Static scan with zero model tokens: `/scan`.
- Review with a verdict per finding: `/review src/`.
- Fix common classes: SQL injection, XSS, command injection, path traversal, unsafe deserialization, hardcoded secrets.
- Authorized pentest and CTF practice with an official security model (Foundation-Sec-8B or WhiteRabbitNeo).

See [Security](SECURITY.md).

## Writing

- Emails and messages: "write email.txt telling the team the update moves to Friday 18:00, max 80 words."
- Summaries: "summarize notes.txt in 3 bullet points with the budget and the deadline."
- Documentation: "write API.md for every public function in lib.py."
- README files, release notes, reports.

Answers use plain, short sentences (ASD-STE100 rules). Text is easy to read for second-language English speakers.

## Study and questions

- Ask about a concept: "what is a race condition? give a 5-line Python example."
- Learn a codebase: "which function in the app package is never called?"
- Practice offline: no internet and no data charges after setup.

## Data tasks

- CSV and JSON reports: "write report.py that prints total sales per region."
- Log analysis: "count status codes and the top IP in access.log."
- Config edits: "set debug to false in settings.json."

## Proof

Every use case above is a challenge in the litecode test suite. See which models pass which tasks on the [Benchmarks](BENCHMARKS.md) page.


---

# Commands

URL: https://konkomaji.github.io/litecode/commands.html

# Commands

## Shell commands

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `litecode` | interactive session in the current folder |
| `litecode "TASK"` | run one task, then exit |
| `litecode setup` | wizard: folders, engine, models |
| `litecode tune [ROLE...]` | measure speed, save best threads and speculative mode |
| `litecode eval [NAME...] [--role R]` | run 8 real agent challenges and score them |
| `litecode doctor` | hardware, config, engine, installed models |
| `litecode init` | create `LITECODE.md` |
| `litecode scan [PATH] [--json]` | static security scan, no model |
| `litecode review [PATH]` | scan, then model verdict per finding |
| `litecode plan "TASK"` | read-only plan |
| `litecode skills` | list skills |
| `litecode skills new NAME` | create a skill step by step |
| `litecode skills rm NAME` | delete a user or project skill |
| `litecode mcp` | list MCP servers (`--tools` to list their tools) |
| `litecode mcp add NAME CMD [ARGS...]` | add an MCP server to the user config |
| `litecode mcp rm NAME` | remove it |
| `litecode learn export FILE [--all]` | write a fine-tune dataset (rated tasks; `--all` adds unrated) |
| `litecode config` | show all settings |
| `litecode config KEY VALUE` | set one setting (`roles.code NAME.gguf` for roles) |
| `litecode fim` | autocomplete server for editors |
| `litecode --version` | version |

Flags: `--yes` (approve all), `--readonly`, `--role NAME`, `--plan`.

## Slash commands (in a session)

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `/help` | list commands |
| `/plan TASK` | plan with no edits, then ask to run it |
| `/review [PATH]` | security review |
| `/scan [PATH]` | static scan only |
| `/test [CMD]` | run tests; if they fail, fix and run again (max 3 rounds) |
| `/diff` | `git diff` |
| `/commit` | model writes a commit message; you confirm before commit |
| `/model [ROLE]` | show roles, or force one (`auto` = router decides) |
| `/mode [ask\|auto\|readonly]` | permission mode |
| `/remember TEXT` | save a project fact |
| `/prefer TEXT` | save a preference for all projects |
| `/memory` | show preferences and facts |
| `/forget [facts\|prefs]` | delete memory (both if no argument) |
| `/good`, `/bad` | rate the last answer |
| `/undo PATH` | restore the newest checkpoint of a file |
| `/sessions` | list sessions in this project |
| `/resume [ID]` | continue a session (latest if no ID) |
| `/clear` | start a new session |
| `/init` | create `LITECODE.md` |
| `/skills` | list skills |
| `/skill new NAME` | create a skill step by step |
| `/skill make DESCRIPTION` | model drafts a skill; you confirm |
| `/skill rm NAME` | delete a skill |
| `/NAME [TASK]` | run skill NAME |
| `/mcp` | list MCP tools |
| `/config [KEY VALUE]` | show or set config |
| `/cost` | tokens and model time this session |
| `/exit` | quit (saves cache, extracts facts) |

## Config keys

| Key | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `engine` | `<home>/engine/llama-server` | llama.cpp server binary |
| `models_dir` | `<home>/models` | GGUF folder |
| `data_dir` | `~/.litecode` | cache, slots, scratch, memory, skills |
| `project_memory` | `project` | `project` or `central` |
| `threads` | 4 | CPU threads |
| `ctx` | 8192 | context tokens |
| `kv_type` | `q8_0` | KV cache type |
| `cache_ram_mb` | 1024 | server prompt cache RAM |
| `gpu_layers` | 0 | layers on GPU (GPU builds only) |
| `speculative` | `auto` | `auto`, `off`, `ngram-simple`, `ngram-mod` |
| `kv_persist` | true | save prompt cache per project |
| `permission` | `ask` | default permission mode |
| `auto_learn` | true | extract facts at session end |
| `lora` | empty | LoRA adapter path |
| `max_steps` | 24 | tool steps per task |
| `temperature` | 0.1 | sampling temperature |
| `port`, `fim_port` | 8080, 8081 | local ports |
| `roles.<role>` | see config | model file per role: code, chat, fim, security, quality |

# Security review

URL: https://konkomaji.github.io/litecode/security.html

# Security review

litecode finds security problems in two stages. Stage 1 costs no model tokens. Stage 2 uses the model only on the flagged lines.

## Stage 1: static scan

```
litecode scan            # whole project
litecode scan src/api    # one folder
litecode scan --json     # machine-readable output
```

litecode runs:

1. Semgrep, if installed (`pip install semgrep`).
2. Bandit, if installed (`pip install bandit`).
3. Built-in rules, always. They need no install and no internet.

Built-in rules cover Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, PHP, and secrets in any file:

| Class | CWE | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| SQL injection | CWE-89 | SQL built with f-strings, `$_GET` in queries |
| Command injection | CWE-78 | `shell=True`, `os.system`, PHP `system()` |
| Code injection | CWE-95 | `eval`, `exec`, `new Function` |
| XSS | CWE-79 | `innerHTML =`, `document.write`, `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` |
| Unsafe deserialization | CWE-502 | `pickle.loads`, `yaml.load`, PHP `unserialize` |
| File inclusion | CWE-98 | `include($_GET[...])` |
| Hardcoded secrets | CWE-798 | API keys, AWS keys, private keys |
| Weak crypto and TLS | CWE-328, CWE-295 | MD5/SHA1, `verify=False` |

## Stage 2: model review

```
litecode review src/
```

For each finding, the model reads about 13 lines around the flagged line. It answers in exactly 4 lines:

```
VERDICT: real | false-positive | needs-context
SEVERITY: high | medium | low
WHY: one sentence
FIX: the smallest safe change
```

A grammar forces this format, so small models cannot drift into long text. The report is saved in `.litecode/reviews/`.

## Fixing

Ask in plain words: "fix the SQL injection in db.py with a parameterized query." litecode edits the code and you approve the diff. Run your tests after: `/test`.

## Security models

`litecode setup` can install an official security model:

- Foundation-Sec-8B (Cisco): analysis, triage, CVE knowledge.
- WhiteRabbitNeo-V3-7B: offensive security and exploit research.

Security tasks route to it automatically when it is installed.

## Rules of use

Use litecode security features only on code and systems that you own or have written permission to test. The model refuses attacks on third parties.


---

# Memory and learning

URL: https://konkomaji.github.io/litecode/memory.html

# Memory and learning

litecode saves every session to disk. It gets better with use in three ways. None of them change the model weights.

## What is saved, and where

| Data | File | Scope |
|---|---|---|
| Every turn of every session | `<project>/.litecode/sessions/<id>.jsonl` | project |
| Full history before compaction | `sessions/<id>.full.jsonl.bak` | project |
| Summary of older turns | `summaries/<id>.md` | project |
| Project facts | `memory.jsonl` | project |
| File snapshots for undo | `checkpoints/` | project |
| Security review reports | `reviews/` | project |
| Your preferences | `<data_dir>/profile.jsonl` | all projects |
| Finished tasks + ratings | `<data_dir>/learn/examples.jsonl` | all projects |

If `project_memory = "central"`, the project files go to `<data_dir>/projects/<name>-<id>/` instead of the project folder.

All files are plain JSON lines or Markdown. You can read, edit or delete them.

## How litecode learns

1. Preferences. A message line that starts with "always", "never", "don't", "prefer", "from now on", "make sure to" or "avoid" becomes a preference. No model call is needed. Preferences go into every prompt, in all projects. Add one by hand: `/prefer use pathlib, not os.path`.
2. Facts. A test command that passes is saved at once. When a session ends (`/exit`), the model reads the session and saves up to 6 durable facts. To turn off the model step: `litecode config auto_learn false`.
3. Examples. Each finished task is saved with the files it changed. For a new task, litecode finds similar past tasks by keyword overlap. It adds the best one to the prompt. Rate answers with `/good` and `/bad`. A bad answer is never reused. A good answer ranks higher.

Context limits: small models have small context windows. litecode keeps the last 8 turns raw. It folds older turns into a summary.

## Fine-tuning (optional, on other hardware)

Constraint: training a 2B+ model on a 4-core CPU takes days. Do it on a GPU machine. A free Google Colab GPU is enough for a LoRA on a 2B-4B model.

1. Rate answers with `/good` while you work.
2. Export: `litecode learn export my_data.jsonl` (add `--all` to include unrated tasks).
3. Train a LoRA on the same base model you use (for example with Unsloth or PEFT). The file is chat format: `{"messages": [...]}` per line.
4. Convert the adapter to GGUF with llama.cpp: `python convert_lora_to_gguf.py --base <base model dir> <adapter dir>`.
5. Copy the `.gguf` adapter to your PC.
6. Set it: `litecode config lora D:/llm/adapters/my-lora.gguf`.
7. Restart litecode. The server loads the adapter.

Warning: an adapter works only with the base model it was trained on.

## Privacy

Nothing leaves your PC. litecode makes no network calls except `litecode setup` downloads, and MCP servers that you add yourself.


---

# Skills

URL: https://konkomaji.github.io/litecode/skills.html

# Skills

A skill is a saved set of steps for one kind of task. litecode adds the steps to the prompt when the skill runs. Small models follow short numbered steps well.

## Use a skill

- `/NAME TASK` runs a skill. Example: `/review src/api/`.
- A skill also runs automatically when its trigger words appear in your message. Max 2 skills per task.
- `/skills` lists all skills with their scope.

## Built-in skills

| Skill | Use |
|---|---|
| `review` | security review: scan, confirm, fix |
| `test-fix` | run tests, fix failures, repeat |
| `explain` | explain code in simple steps |
| `commit` | commit message from the diff |
| `refactor` | change structure, keep behavior, run tests |
| `skill-builder` | design a new skill with the model's help |

## Make a skill

Option 1, step by step:

```
/skill new django-migrations
```

litecode asks for a description, trigger words, and the steps.

Option 2, the model drafts it:

```
/skill make a skill that checks Django migrations for missing indexes
```

litecode shows the draft. You confirm before it saves.

Option 3, write the file yourself. Create `.litecode/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`:

```
---
name: django-migrations
description: Check new Django migrations for missing indexes and data loss.
triggers: migration, migrations, django
tools: glob, read_file, grep
---
1. Find new files with glob "**/migrations/*.py".
2. Read each new migration.
3. Flag RemoveField and DeleteModel. They lose data.
4. Flag ForeignKey fields without db_index on large tables.
5. In final, list each problem as file:line and a fix.
```

Rules for the file:

- `name`: 2-41 characters. Lowercase letters, digits, `-`, `_`.
- `description`: one sentence.
- `triggers`: comma separated words (optional).
- `tools`: tools the steps use (optional, for the reader).
- Body: 3-8 numbered steps. Use simple words. Name the tools.

## Scope

| Scope | Folder | Who sees it |
|---|---|---|
| project | `<project>/.litecode/skills/` | this project; commit it to share with your team |
| user | `<data_dir>/skills/` | all your projects |
| builtin | shipped with litecode | everyone |

On a name clash, project wins over user, and user wins over builtin.

Delete: `/skill rm NAME`. Built-in skills cannot be deleted. Override one with a project skill of the same name.


---

# MCP servers

URL: https://konkomaji.github.io/litecode/mcp.html

# MCP servers

litecode is an MCP client. It starts MCP servers over stdio and gives their tools to the model. It reads the same `mcpServers` format as Claude Code.

## Add a server

Command line:

```
litecode mcp add fs npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem .
litecode mcp add git uvx mcp-server-git
litecode mcp                 # list servers
litecode mcp --tools         # start them and list their tools
litecode mcp rm fs
```

Or edit a config file:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "fs": {"command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem", "."]},
    "notes": {"command": "python", "args": ["notes_server.py"], "env": {"NOTES_DIR": "D:/notes"}},
    "off": {"command": "x", "disabled": true}
  }
}
```

Config files (later wins on a name clash):

1. `<data_dir>/mcp.json` (user, written by `litecode mcp add`)
2. `<project>/.mcp.json` (project, same file Claude Code uses)
3. `<project>/.litecode/mcp.json`

## How the model calls a tool

Tools appear as `mcp__<server>__<tool>`. The model uses the normal JSON format:

```
{"tool": "mcp__fs__read_file", "args": {"path": "README.md"}}
```

Each MCP call asks for approval in `ask` mode. In `readonly` mode MCP calls are refused.

## Limits

- Transport: stdio only. HTTP/SSE servers are not supported yet.
- Tools only. MCP resources and prompts are not used yet.
- litecode shows the model at most 20 MCP tools. Small models choose badly from long lists. Add only what you need.
- A server that fails to start is skipped. litecode prints the error and continues.
- Most MCP servers need Node.js (`npx`) or `uv` (`uvx`). Install those first. Offline use needs the server installed locally.


---

# Editor autocomplete

URL: https://konkomaji.github.io/litecode/editors.html

# Editor autocomplete

litecode can serve fill-in-the-middle (FIM) autocomplete with the small `fim` model (default Qwen2.5-Coder-1.5B, about 20 tokens/s on a 4-core CPU).

## 1. Start the server

```
litecode fim
```

It listens on `http://127.0.0.1:8081/infill`. Change the port with `litecode config fim_port 8082`.

RAM: the fim model uses about 1.5 GB. It can run next to the main model on a 16 GB PC.

## 2. VS Code

The extension is in `editors/vscode/`. It has no dependencies.

1. Copy the folder `editors/vscode` to `~/.vscode/extensions/litecode-complete` (Windows: `%USERPROFILE%\.vscode\extensions\litecode-complete`).
2. Restart VS Code.
3. Type code. A grey suggestion appears after you stop typing. Press Tab to accept.

Settings (`litecode.*`): `url`, `maxTokens` (48), `debounceMs` (350), `enabled`.

## 3. Other editors

Any editor plugin that supports the llama.cpp `/infill` API works. Example: `llama.vim` and `llama.vscode` by ggml-org. Point it at the URL above.

Test by hand:

```
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8081/infill -d '{"input_prefix":"def add(a, b):\n    ","input_suffix":"\n","n_predict":16}'
```

# FAQ

URL: https://konkomaji.github.io/litecode/faq.html

# FAQ

## What is litecode?

litecode is a free, open-source AI coding and security assistant that runs on your own computer. It works in the terminal like a cloud coding agent, but it uses open-weight models through llama.cpp. After setup it works fully offline.

## Can I run an AI coding assistant without a GPU?

Yes. litecode runs on CPU only. On a 2019 Ryzen 3 3200G with 16 GB RAM, the default 2B model writes about 15 tokens per second and passed 8 of 8 coding tasks in our tests.

## How much RAM do I need?

4 GB is the minimum. 8 GB is comfortable for daily coding. 16 GB runs 8B-class models. 32 GB or a GPU runs 30B-class models. See [Hardware and models](HARDWARE.md).

## Does litecode work on high-end machines too?

Yes. litecode scales up. With an NVIDIA GPU it installs the CUDA engine and moves the model to the GPU. With 32 GB or more it loads bigger models. Low-end support is the floor, not the limit.

## Is it really offline and private?

Yes. After setup, litecode makes no network calls. Your code, prompts, and memory stay on your disk as plain files. MCP servers that you add yourself can use the network.

## Which models does it use?

It picks from a tested catalog: MiniCPM5-2B, Qwen2.5-Coder, Qwen3.5, LFM2.5-8B-A1B, Llama 3.2, Gemma 4, Foundation-Sec-8B, WhiteRabbitNeo, Ministral, and bigger models for GPUs. Any GGUF model works.

## How is litecode different from Ollama or LM Studio?

Ollama and LM Studio run models. litecode is a coding agent: it reads and edits your files, runs your tests, reviews security, remembers your project, and tunes itself to your hardware. It uses llama.cpp directly with low-RAM settings.

## Does it learn from me?

Yes, without retraining. It saves your preferences, project facts, and rated past answers, and reuses them. You can also export a dataset and train a LoRA adapter on a GPU machine. See [Memory and learning](MEMORY.md).

## Can it do more than coding?

Yes. Coding and security are the main focus. It also writes emails, summaries, and documentation, answers study questions, and handles CSV, JSON, and log data. See [Use cases](USE-CASES.md).

## Does it support MCP and skills like Claude Code?

Yes. It reads the same `.mcp.json` format and supports `SKILL.md` skills with project, user, and built-in scopes. See [MCP servers](MCP.md) and [Skills](SKILLS.md).

## Why are the answers so short?

litecode follows ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English: answer first, short sentences, exact values, no filler. Short answers cost fewer tokens, so they arrive faster on slow machines. You can change the rules in `SYSTEM.md`.

## Is it free?

Yes. litecode is MIT licensed. Models are open-weight; check each model's license before you redistribute it.

## Who built it?

Konko Maji. Contact: [work.konkomaji@gmail.com](mailto:work.konkomaji@gmail.com), [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/konkomaji/), [X](https://x.com/konkomaji).


---

# Troubleshooting

URL: https://konkomaji.github.io/litecode/troubleshooting.html

# Troubleshooting

Run `litecode doctor` first. It shows the engine, folders and models.

| Problem | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `engine not found` | no llama-server | `litecode setup`, or `litecode config engine PATH` |
| `no model for role 'x'` | model file missing | `litecode setup`, or `litecode config roles.x FILE.gguf` |
| `llama-server exited during startup` | not enough RAM, or bad model file | close programs; use a smaller model; download the file again |
| First answer is slow | model loads from disk, prompt is processed | normal. Next tasks are faster. Keep models on an SSD if possible |
| Output is garbage (`GGGG...`) | broken model file or engine bug for that model | check the file hash against Hugging Face; try another quant or a newer engine |
| `(model broke protocol, retrying)` | small model wrote text, not JSON | normal now and then. If constant, use a bigger model with `/model quality` |
| `litecode` command not found | Python scripts folder not on PATH | use `python -m litecode.cli`, or add the folder to PATH |
| Commands fail on Windows with WSL errors | `bash` resolves to the WSL stub | litecode uses Git Bash or PowerShell. Install Git for Windows for bash |
| PC freezes, disk light on | RAM is full, Windows swaps | use a smaller model, lower `ctx`, close the browser |
| Port in use | another server on 8080 | `litecode config port 8090` |
| MCP server fails | missing `npx`/`uvx`, or bad args | run the server command by hand to see the error |
| Wrong answers repeat | a bad example is reused | `/bad` after a bad answer; `/forget` to clear facts |

Logs: run the engine by hand to see its errors:

```
<engine> -m <models_dir>/<model>.gguf -c 4096
```
